standard_prerequisites.name: Henselization of a local ring, its flatness, and the identity (A/p)^h = A^h/pA^h
standard_prerequisites.use: Is what identifies the unique minimal prime of A^h with the extension of that of A.

standard_prerequisites.name: Unibranchness as locality of the integral closure of the reduced quotient
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the equivalent form of the conclusion that the direct proof establishes.

standard_prerequisites.name: Integrality, going up, and flat base change of a chain of ring inclusions
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the chain of inclusions over A^h whose maximal ideals give the contradiction.

core_obligations: Note that the statement follows from the branch lemma but give a direct proof, and record that the residue field kappa = A/m agrees with the residue field of A^h (proof lines 31261-31265).
Assume (2) and let p^h be the unique minimal prime of A^h; use flatness of A -> A^h and going down to conclude that p = A cap p^h is the unique minimal prime of A (proof lines 31268-31272).
Use A^h/pA^h = (A/p)^h together with the reducedness of the henselization to conclude p^h = pA^h (proof lines 31273-31276).

Let A' be the integral closure of A/p in its fraction field; unibranchness requires A' to be local, so suppose instead that A' has distinct maximal ideals m_1, m_2, note that A -> A' is integral so every maximal ideal of A' lies over m, and choose f_i in m_i with f_i not in m_{3-i} (proof lines 31277-31284).
Pass to the finite subalgebra B = A/p[f_1, f_2] contained in A', which has the two distinct maximal ideals B cap m_i (proof lines 31285-31286).

Tensor the inclusions A/p in B in kappa(p) with the flat map A -> A^h to obtain the chain A^h/p^h in B tensor_A A^h in kappa(p) tensor_A A^h in kappa(p^h), the last inclusion because kappa(p) tensor_A A^h is a localization of the domain A^h/p^h (proof lines 31287-31301).

Derive the contradiction from the two distinct maximal ideals of B tensor_A A^h lying over the unique maximal ideal of the domain A^h/p^h, concluding that A' is local and hence that A is unibranch (remainder of the counted proof span).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that for a local ring A with henselization A^h, A is unibranch if and only if A^h has a unique minimal prime (source lines 31248-31259). The proof notes that this follows from the branch count but supplies a direct argument anyway, and the direct argument is what is counted. Assume (2) and let p^h be the unique minimal prime of A^h: flatness of A -> A^h makes p = A cap p^h the unique minimal prime of A by going down, and since A^h/pA^h = (A/p)^h is reduced by the reducedness lemma, one gets p^h = pA^h (proof lines 31268-31276). Then with A' the integral closure of A/p in its fraction field, unibranchness amounts to A' being local; the proof argues by contradiction, noting that A -> A' is integral so every maximal ideal of A' lies over m, and that if A' had two distinct maximal ideals m_1 and m_2 one could choose f_i in m_i outside m_{3-i} and pass to the finite subalgebra B = A/p[f_1, f_2] with the two distinct maximal ideals B cap m_i (proof lines 31277-31286). The substantive step is the tensor comparison: the inclusions A/p in B in kappa(p) become after tensoring with the flat map A -> A^h the chain A^h/p^h in B tensor_A A^h in kappa(p) tensor_A A^h in kappa(p^h), the last inclusion because kappa(p) tensor_A A^h = kappa(p) tensor_{A/p} A^h/p^h is a localization of the domain A^h/p^h (proof lines 31287-31301 and following). The contradiction is then produced from the two distinct maximal ideals of B tensor_A A^h lying over the single maximal ideal of the domain A^h/p^h. The non-routine content is this flat base change comparison, which converts a statement about A' into one about the tensor product over A^h.
